why: Sort the levels; then a class is a contiguous run whose max minus min is at most maxSpread. Greedily start a class at the lowest unplaced level and pack everyone within maxSpread of it, which is the classic 'cover points with fixed-length intervals'.
hints: Order does not matter for grouping, so sort the levels. Who should share a class with the weakest trainee?
The lowest level must be in some class; that class can include everyone up to lowest + maxSpread, and taking all of them never hurts. Then repeat from the next uncovered level.
Sort, walk once, and open a new class whenever level - anchor > maxSpread, setting anchor to that level. O(n log n) time.
pitfalls: The condition is max - min <= maxSpread inside a class, so compare with the class's first (smallest) level, not the previous one.
maxSpread = 0 means only equal levels can share a class.
constraints:
• 1 <= n <= 10^5
  • 1 <= levels[i] <= 10^9
  • 0 <= maxSpread <= 10^9
  • Not stated in the source; reasonable bounds.
